newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares ease after hitting resistance.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares ease after hitting resistance.

text.p: Istanbul shares eased slightly in quiet trade on Tuesday as players took profits after the index failed to pierce fresh resistance seen at 2,050 level following the recent string of records, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed at 2,036, down seven points, or 0.34 percent from Monday's all-time high close of 2,043. It brushed a trading record of 2,061 in the morning.
Daily trade volume shrank 25 percent to 28.26 trillion lira from Monday's 37.64 trillion.

"Trade became weaker in the afternoon session. Bluechip utilities and state shares had put on high premiums during the recent rally, so they did not have much room to carry the index further up," said Sinan Paksoy from Prim securities.
State shares have major impact on the market index because of their high market capitalisations.
"The index might ease a bit more but I do not expect it to go below the 2,010 support," he added.
The index had rallied 30.5 percent, hitting 10 records to Monday's close from June 18 on hopes about the new government after the former Islamist-led coalition government resigned.
"The market may go into sideways trend and continue its slight rise amid six-month profit prospects of firms," said Serap Gunes from Tacirler Securities.

Of the 247 shares traded, 119 declined, 82 advanced and 46 finished stable. The IMKB Industrial edged up 0.15 percent to 1,949, the IMKB Services firmed 0.26 percent to 1,955 and the IMKB Financial eased 0.72 percent to 2,191.
The index representing the tourism sector was the leading loser with a 3.92 percent fall.

Actives were led by largely state-owned flat steel maker Eregli, down 500 lira at 26,500, petroleum products marketer Petrol Ofisi, down 1,000 lira at 32,000 and utilities Aktas Elektrik, up 5,000 lira at 270,000 and Cukurova Elektrik, steady at 275,000 lira.
They made up 21.8 percent of the total turnover.
